text:
The results above include the source's i.i.d. and general finite-row
central limit theorems, both array proof routes, the calculations of
Examples 3.4.5--3.4.13, Exercises 3.4.1--3.4.13, Erd\H{o}s--Kac, and
the full Berry--Esseen proof with Lemmas 3.4.18--3.4.19.
The source's remarks that surround these results are stated, with every
mathematical claim in them proved, in
\cref{sec:p15-w02c-p15-015-reading}: the reason for the letter \(\chi\)
(\cref{thm:p15-w02c-p15-015-chi-square}); the roulette wheel and bet of
Example 3.4.5 (\cref{def:p15-w02c-p15-015-roulette}); the histogram
correction of Example 3.4.7, its \(\mathbb P(S_{16}\leq11.5)\) reading and its
consistency (\cref{thm:p15-w02c-p15-015-histogram}), and the comparison
of \(0.1974\) with the exact \(0.1964\)
(\cref{def:p15-w02c-p15-015-sixteen-tosses}); the contrast with the
pairwise strong law opening Example 3.4.9
(\cref{thm:p15-w02c-p15-015-pairwise-contrast}); the truncation-level
rationale of Example 3.4.13 (\cref{thm:p15-w02c-p15-015-truncation-window})
and the following Remark on tails \(x^{-\alpha}\), \(0<\alpha<2\)
(\cref{thm:p15-w02c-p15-015-power-tail-limit}); the opening remark of
Section 3.4.3 on \(\exp(e^4)\) (\cref{sec:p15-w02c-p15-015-erdos-kac-scale});
and the Berry--Esseen remarks on van Beek's constant, Feller's
assessment, the third moment, Heyde (1967) and Hall (1982)
(\cref{sec:p15-w02c-p15-015-berry-esseen-remarks}).
The source attributes the normal-domain criterion, Theorem~3.4.14, to
L\'evy, gives no proof, and refers to Gnedenko and Kolmogorov (1954),
which it describes as the definitive account of many questions about
sums of independent variables (\cref{sec:p15-w02c-p15-015-levy-criterion}).
The criterion is proved in
\cref{thm:p15-nda-characterization}. For an i.i.d. law that is nondegenerate,
meaning not concentrated at a single point, it
characterizes the existence of deterministic \(a_n\in\mathbb R\),
\(b_n>0\), with \((S_n-a_n)/b_n\Rightarrow\chi\), by
\[
 \frac{y^2\mathbb P(|X_1|>y)}
      {\mathbb E(X_1^2;|X_1|\leq y)}\longrightarrow0.
 \]
Its denominator is used only for sufficiently large \(y\) where
it is positive. Both directions and all admissible center/scale
choices are supplied there; \cref{thm:p15-nda-normalizer-construction}
constructs the normalizers. The exact 1954 Section~35 cutoff route is
\cref{thm:p15-nda-gk-cutoff-route}, with its complete i.i.d. interface.
The broader original general-array and canonical-measure presentations
are distinguished in \cref{def:p15-nda-historical-boundary}.
Heyde's equivalence and van Beek's constant are reported by the source
without proof, and are stated as such in
\cref{sec:p15-w02c-p15-015-berry-esseen-remarks}. The later local-limit
and stable-law sections of the source are separate presentations.

anchor_quote: and let \(\chi\) denote a variable with this standard normal law.
text:
The letter is chosen because the square of a standard normal variable
has the chi-squared law with one degree of freedom
(\cref{thm:p15-w02c-p15-015-chi-square}).

characteristic-function criteria, moment problems and section exercises
are supplied in \cref{sec:p15-characteristic-function-criteria-and-moments},

moment-method hypothesis), which is
\cref{thm:p15-w02c-p15-012-bound-gives-growth}.
